independence: Independently read the complete three-page IW primary report and all sixteen submission pages; checked addressed bill title and Article 5 proposed CO 2 KostAufG 5 a onpp 63–64 and explanationp 124. Rendered and visually checked submissionphysicalp 3 and IWpp 1 and 3.

checks.result: The submission places the low/lower-middle income qualification inside an explicit explanatory dash clause before the 14.5-to 25.2 figures. IWdefinition 1 has the 10%energy-spending condition without an income restriction; definition 3 combines this with relative-poor/lower-middle income and gives 11.3-to 16.8. The narrow source-definition mismatch is supported.

The income phrase could describe those especially vulnerable rather than announce an exact statistical restriction. But the explanatory syntax presents it as a definition, not merely a list of especially exposed groups. Keep this alternative; minor is more defensible than major because the statistic is introductory and all measures rise.

IWheadline itself speaks of households while body speaks of persons in private households. Do not blame the submission for repeating that source-headline wording or present 16.8 as a new corrected household-weighted rate. This caveat must remain prominent.

Neither 16.8 nor 25.2 is a within-low-income-group incidence rate. They are overall population shares satisfying different conditions in IW. Avoid language implying the correct share of low-income households affected is 16.8. The current candidate is broadly careful but card wording can be made more explicit.

2021–2022 figures extrapolate 2020 SOEPdata using price/income indices; the primary excludes relief packages and notes heterogeneity/behavioural adjustment. These are not measured current hardship rates. This matters to limits but does not negate the two-definition distinction.

The submission explicitly requests a technology-neutral heating-cost cap onphysicalp 14/printed 13, after welcoming existing proposed tenant cost-sharing safeguards. A higher vulnerable-share presentation adds support to stronger protections; directiontrue is reasonable. It does not establish the cap is wrong or unnecessary.

required_wording_limits: Keep the finding narrowly about combining an income-restricted definition with the broader definition’s figures.
Do not turn the issue into an allegation that energy poverty did not rise.
Do not give 16.8 as an actual corrected national household rate or a within-subgroup incidence rate.
Preserve the source’s own household/person headline mismatch and extrapolation/relief limitations.

history.event: Independent primary-source and full-context review completed; retain minor/true with denominator/source-definition limits.
